title: The Periodic Table
seo_title: SSS 1 Chemistry: The Periodic Table Worksheets (WAEC/NECO)
standard_text: The position of elements in the periodic table and their electron configurations; groups and periods; periodic trends in atomic radius, ionisation energy, electron affinity and electronegativity; similarities in the chemical properties of elements in the same group. (summary of the senior secondary Chemistry curriculum, SSS 1; WAEC and NECO syllabuses)
meta_desc: Free SSS 1 Chemistry worksheets (senior secondary curriculum, WAEC and NECO): organising the periodic table, groups and valence electrons, families of elements, periodic trends and trends in properties. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Elements in a group have the same number of valence electrons.
key_sub: Atomic radius increases down a group and decreases across a period.
body_html:
How to think about it

The periodic table arranges elements by atomic number. Elements in the same group have similar chemical properties because they have the same number of valence electrons: alkali metals (group 1), halogens (group 17) and noble gases (group 18).

Across a period the nuclear charge increases, so atoms get smaller and ionisation energy and electronegativity increase. Down a group extra energy levels are added, so atoms get bigger and ionisation energy decreases.

Example

Which is larger, Na or Cl?

Same period; Cl has more protons pulling the electrons in.

Answer: Na

Example

Why are the noble gases unreactive?

Look at the outer energy level.

Answer: their outer energy level is full

Common mistakes

  • Thinking atoms get bigger across a period.
  • Mixing up groups (columns) and periods (rows).
  • Thinking the halogens are metals.
